title: LEO latent composition of known skills
hypothesis: For additive task families with independently trained skill factors, composing two learned 2D latent task codes and decoding once matches direct task-vector addition within 1.10x held-out query NRMSE, and is smaller in actual amortized inference bytes at N=20.
physical_object: shared meta-trained base function plus reusable skill latent factors
mirror_coordinate: sum of two learned 2D skill coordinates, decoded through shared structured Mirror map
logical_multiplicity: unseen pairwise compositions of known skill directions
controls: shared base with no task code
direct task-vector arithmetic (sum of learned skill deltas)
LEO generic latent decoder with summed skill latents
structured Mirror decoder with summed skill latents

development.selection_metric: mean held-out-pair query NRMSE at step 5

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror composed-task NRMSE <= 1.10x direct task-vector arithmetic and Mirror total amortized inference bytes at N=20 are lower than direct arithmetic; report all worlds and per-pair outcomes.
failure_gate: Any world misses quality/byte gate, generic LEO matches or beats Mirror at similar bytes, or composition requires pair-specific learned state.
boundaries: Synthetic aligned additive linear skill screen only.
Skill pair identities are held out from all meta-training and development.
Combinatorial count is not claimed as independent capacity.
Task-vector arithmetic and any decoder, index, or composition state are fully charged.
